reference_images: Reference image 1 is the fishmonger's character sheet: use it ONLY for his exact face, build, grey hair, navy knit jumper, navy oilskin bib apron and black wellington boots. Do not reproduce the sheet's panel layout or title.

Reference image 2 is the walrus's creature sheet: use it ONLY for its exact size and shape: a subadult walrus about 2.0-2.3 m long, grey-brown wrinkled skin, dense white whisker pad, SMALL just-emerging tusks (not long adult tusks), no external ears. Do not reproduce the sheet's panel layout or its printed text.

Reference image 3 is the delivery van's prop sheet: use it ONLY for the van's exact look: small kei-truck-proportioned white cab, white refrigerated box body with the refrigeration unit on the front of the box, roller-shutter rear door, hydraulic tail lift folded flat under the rear sill. Do not reproduce the sheet's panel layout.

Reference image 4 is the environment sheet for this Scottish harbour quay. Panel 1, CAMERA POV, is exactly what the camera sees in every frame. Panel 2, TOP-DOWN VIEW, shows the van's path (orange arrow): in from the right along the near side of the road, then a right turn into the centre parking space, nose to the water. The other panels are spatial reference only and are never the camera view.
overall_summary: Fixed harbourside CCTV looking out over a Scottish harbour quay. A fishmonger's small white refrigerated van drives in from the right, turns right and parks nose-in in the empty space directly in front of the camera, rear door facing the camera. He gets out, rolls the rear door up and finds a walrus lying in the crushed ice, surrounded by fish heads: it ate the whole delivery. He jumps back. The walrus burps, slumps out onto the road in a cascade of ice and fish heads, and heaves off to the left toward the slipway down to the water. This storyboard is Clip 1 and ends with the walrus at the top of the slipway.
tone: Unplanned real-life security-camera footage: ordinary, observational, deadpan and believable, never cinematic, staged, polished, promotional or commercial.
capture_style: A fixed, wall-mounted CCTV security camera about 3 m up, wide-angle lens with only mild curvature, slightly soft ordinary CCTV image quality and natural exposure. Completely locked off: no operator, no handheld movement, no pan, tilt or zoom.
visual_style: Authentic harbourside CCTV footage, wide fixed framing, flat overcast midday light, damp stone and wet tarmac, muted grey-blue harbour palette, documentary realism.
visual_realism: Real-world documentary observation with natural overcast light, a real working Scottish harbour, realistic vehicle and animal motion and real-world scale, no professional colour grade or advertising polish.
audio_policy: Atmospheric location sound and physical foley only: the van's engine and door, the roller shutter rattling up, the walrus's burp and grunts, crushed ice sliding and clattering onto tarmac, the fishmonger's startled wordless exclamation, gulls and lapping water.
camera_lock: The exact CAMERA POV of reference image 4, panel 1, in all six frames: same position, height, wide angle, framing, horizon and background. The harbour road runs left-right across the lower frame and continues off both edges; the nose-in parking row sits beyond it with the empty centre space directly in front of the camera; the stone quay wall with a black iron railing runs across the frame beyond the parking row; the slipway is at the far left; moored boats, the stone breakwater (left) and the far-shore whitewashed and stone cottages (right) sit in the distance. No cuts, pans, tilts, zooms or alternate views. ZOOM IS IDENTICAL IN ALL SIX PANELS: the boats, breakwater, cottages, quay wall, parking lines and hatchback are exactly the same size and in exactly the same place in panel 6 as in panel 1. Panels 4-6 are NOT closer or tighter than panels 1-3.
continuity_invariants: Exactly one fishmonger, one walrus and one delivery van; the only other vehicle is the dark hatchback parked nose-in two spaces to the LEFT of the centre space, which never moves.
The van comes in from off-frame right along the NEAR side of the road, turns right across the road, and parks nose-in in the centre space; once parked it never moves again.

Parked van orientation by literal visible parts: its front bumper, headlights and windscreen face the WATER (away from the camera); its rear bumper, roller-shutter rear door and folded tail lift face the CAMERA, square-on.
The walrus is inside the closed cargo box from the start and becomes visible only when the rear door is rolled up; it never appears from nowhere.
The walrus is a subadult about 2.0-2.3 m long: it looks huge inside the cargo box, filling most of it, and is about as long as the fishmonger is tall, lying down.
The roller-shutter door rolls UP into the top of the box; it is not a hinged or barn door.
The hydraulic tail lift stays folded flat under the rear sill in every frame; it is never lowered or used.
The fishmonger gets out of the driver's door on the camera-RIGHT side of the van (UK right-hand drive).
Only ice and fish heads spill out: no blood anywhere.
The stack of blue fish boxes and rope stays by the quay wall to the right of the centre space throughout.

REAL-WORLD SCALE IN THE WIDE FRAME: the van's rear is about 8 m from the camera, so the fishmonger at the van is small in the frame, a normal 1.8 m adult whose head is level with the top of the van's box body, about one-fifth of the frame height; he is never drawn as a large foreground figure.

The walrus is about 2.0-2.3 m long: lying on the road it is about as long as the fishmonger is tall and about as tall as his waist; inside the box its body is narrower than the box and fits inside it. It is never bigger than the van's box body.
The dark hatchback stays parked in the same space in all six panels, including panel 6.
The stone slipway at the far left edge of the frame, sloping down into the water, is visible in every panel.

panel_convention: Six chronological landscape panels in 3 columns x 2 rows (frames 1-3 top row, 4-6 bottom row), each with a true 16:9 image area and a clean white caption band beneath with only the frame number and caption. No text inside any image area.
hard_constraints: Keep the exact CAMERA POV framing, horizon, quay wall, parking lines, slipway, boats and background identical in all six panels.
Never show the van in the centre space before frame 3, and never show it moving after frame 3.
Never show the van's front toward the camera once parked; the rear roller door faces the camera.
Never lower or deploy the tail lift.
Never show the walrus before the door is rolled up in frame 4.
Never give the walrus long adult tusks or external ears.
No blood, no gore: only crushed ice and fish heads.
No extra people, no duplicate walrus or van, no camera cuts, teleportation or morphing.
No text, signs, timestamps or logos inside any image area.
Do not turn the storyboard sheet into a video frame, title card or finished cinematic composition.
Never zoom in or crop tighter in any panel; panel 6 has exactly the same framing as panel 1.
Never draw the fishmonger or the walrus larger than real-world scale at this distance; neither is ever a big foreground figure.
Never remove the parked hatchback in any panel.
Never leave the driver's door open after frame 3.
